svg.title: Fault Lines
svg.desc: Fault Lines. How much of a nervous system can be taken away before sensory input no longer reaches the motor system? The male fruit fly central nervous system seen from the front on a black field, its neuropils shaded from dark to bright red by the share of sensory-to-motor flow capacity lost when every cell type anchored in them is removed; the GNG is brightest at 34.7%. 11,751 cell types, 243,439 connections. Routing halves after 4.1% of cell types are removed in order of output synapses, against 28.3% at random.
